key_insight: GEqTrain shows that a single configuration-driven equivariant GNN framework can be retargeted across diverse 3D scientific tasks by changing dataset field mappings, model stacks, and training objectives rather than rewriting the software.
engineering_relevance: This reduces integration and maintenance overhead for computational science workflows by making predictive and generative equivariant models more reusable, reproducible, and easier to adapt to new molecular problems.
method: Map raw data into typed node, edge, and graph fields through a declarative schema.
Assemble equivariant backbones, losses, and training pipelines with Hydra configurations.
Extend the framework with GEqDiff, an equivariant flow-matching generator for Cartesian positions and higher-order fields up to l=3.
evidence_signal: The framework is demonstrated on three tasks in one software stack—coarse-grained to atomistic backmapping, NMR chemical-shift prediction, and equivariant generative modeling—and further validated on a synthetic benchmark for jointly reconstructing heterogeneous equivariant fields.
watch_item: The approach emphasizes flexibility over task-specific optimization, so competitive performance may still lag specialized systems for a given application.
paper_title: GEqTrain: A Configuration-Driven Framework for Retargeting Equivariant Graph Neural Networks Across 3D Scientific Tasks
